title: Compound measures
examples: How do I find the density if I know the mass and volume?
What is the formula for pressure?
Can you show me an example of a rate of flow problem?

explain.say: Today we will look at compound measures in science. These measures combine different basic units. We will learn about density, pressure, and flow rates today.
First we look at density. Density is mass divided by volume. The formula is density equals mass over volume. The unit for density is usually grams per cubic centimeter.

For a concrete example, if something has a mass of sixty grams. And it takes up twenty cubic centimeters. You divide sixty by twenty to find the density. The density is three grams per cubic centimeter.
Next we consider pressure. Pressure is force applied over an area. The formula is pressure equals force divided by area. The unit for pressure is usually Pascals.
For an example, imagine a force of one hundred newtons. This force acts over an area of five square meters. You divide one hundred by five to get a pressure of twenty Pascals.

faq.q: What is the difference between density and mass?
faq.a: Mass is the amount of matter in an object. Density tells you how much mass is packed into a certain space. You can think of it as how tightly packed the stuff is.
asks: Is density the same as weight?

faq.q: Do I need to convert units before calculating pressure?
faq.a: Yes, you must make sure your units match the formula. If force is in Newtons, the area must be in square meters for Pascals.
asks: What units do I use for pressure?
Does area need to be in square units?

faq.q: How do I calculate the rate of flow?
faq.a: Rate of flow is simply volume divided by time. It tells you how much space something moves through each second or minute.
asks: How do I find volume per time?

faq.q: Can I use the density formula for liquids only?
faq.a: No, the density formula works for any substance, solid, liquid, or gas. You just need to measure its mass and its volume correctly.

faq.q: If I change the area, does the pressure change?
faq.a: Yes, pressure is inversely related to area. If you keep the force the same, making the area smaller increases the pressure significantly.
asks: What happens to pressure if area decreases?
Is pressure affected by the surface size?

facts: Density is calculated by dividing mass by volume.
Pressure is defined as force applied perpendicular to an area.
The standard unit for density is often grams per cubic centimeter.
Rate of flow is calculated by dividing volume by time.

quiz.say: A block has a mass of 45 grams and a volume of 15 cubic centimeters. What is its density?
quiz.why: You correctly divided the mass by the volume to find the density.

wrong.1: You multiplied the mass by the volume, which is incorrect for density.
wrong.2: You added the mass and the volume together, which is not the formula.
wrong.3: You only used the volume in the calculation.

quiz.say: A force of 50 Newtons is spread over an area of 10 square meters. What is the pressure?
quiz.why: You correctly divided the force by the area to find the pressure in Pascals.

wrong.0: You subtracted the area from the force, which is not the formula.
wrong.1: You multiplied the force by the area, which is incorrect.
wrong.2: You divided the force by the square of the area.

quiz.say: A pipe fills with 120 liters of water over 4 minutes. What is the rate of flow?
quiz.why: You correctly divided the total volume by the total time to find the rate.

wrong.0: You subtracted the time from the volume, which is not the correct operation.
wrong.1: You multiplied the volume by the time, which gives a different measure.
wrong.2: You divided the volume by the square of the time.
